entities.name: Canon of Medicine (Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb)
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: A five-volume medical encyclopedia composed by Ibn Sina (Avicenna) c. 1025 CE, synthesizing Greek (Hippocratic-Galenic), Indian, and Islamic medical knowledge into a comprehensive, well-organized system. The Canon covers general principles of medicine, simple drugs (760 medicinal plants, minerals, and animal products), diseases organized head-to-toe, systemic diseases (fevers, infections), and pharmacology (compound drugs). Translated into Latin by Gerard of Cremona in the 12th century, it became the standard medical textbook at European universities (Montpellier, Louvain, Padua) and was used continuously until at least the 17th century — making it arguably the most influential medical textbook in human history.
